newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures start higher, turn mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures start higher, turn mixed.

text.p: CME lumber futures opened higher on light short covering, but then quickly turned mixed with selling motivated by lower cash prices and a bearish U.S. home sales report, traders said.
July traded both sides of unchanged early, with short covering appearing to be the primary supportive factor.
"Obviously the home sales report was not terribly constructive," said one analyst.
The U.S. Commerce Department reported April single-family home sales were down 7.7 percent to an annualized rate of 772,000 units the lowest since October.
Also, Random Lengths reported cash spruce prices dropped to $364 per thousand board feet Friday from $377 a week ago.
At 0947 CDT, CME lumber was up $1.320 to down $1.60 per tbf with July up $1.30 at $375.50.
